title: hook and action texts: the save door's literal text-key reader stops at the closing quote, so ctx.text('k' + x) is refused at save as an undeclared literal key 'k'
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgX6mQpVU8yUysiRAFC

Filing gate: **(b) out-of-scope finding** of PR #35686 (Fixes #35512), nit N2 of its contract review (record 7025732554). **Pre-existing on main** for the plain call; #35686 carries the same reader to the `?.(` shape. Dedupe: searched open issues for `TEXT_CALL` concatenation; none.

Suggested-grade: p3 (a false save refusal only on a concatenated key, which the runtime would treat as a computed key) · suggested domain `domain:spec` · area:build · for triage first touch.

## What happens
- `TEXT_CALL` in `packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts` (read through `hookTextKeysAskedIn` by both `HookSchema` and `ActionSchema` save doors) matches `ctx.text(` + quote + snake_case key + the same quote, and stops there.
- So `ctx.text('follow_up' + suffix)` (and, after #35686, `ctx.text?.('follow_up' + suffix)`) is read as a literal ask for `follow_up`. If `texts` does not declare `follow_up` but does declare the keys the expression builds, the save refuses a body that would run correctly; if it declares `follow_up`, the computed key goes unchecked at save, which is the intended run-time half.
- Read on the tree, not run.

## Ask
- The literal reader treats an ask as literal only when the closing quote is followed by `,` or `)` (after optional whitespace); anything else (`+`, a template hole, a member access) is a computed key left to the run-time refusal. Pins: lit (a plain literal still refused when undeclared) and dark (a concatenated key not refused at save), on hooks and actions.
- ⛔ Not a new rule: it makes the save half's "literal" match what the ruling (#34374 6913660232 parameter 7) means by literal.

## Reader
The seat that takes `area:build` authoring-rule cards.
